title: Differentiation rules
examples: When I have a function like three x squared plus x, how do I find the derivative?
If I have two terms added together, do I differentiate them separately?
What if the term has a constant number times x, like five x?

explain.say: Today we learn three rules for differentiation. These rules help us find the derivative of various functions. We start with the power rule for differentiation. This rule tells us how to differentiate x to a power. The power rule says that the derivative of x to the power of n is n x to the power of n minus one.

Let us try an example using the power rule. Find the derivative of x to the power of four. We use the power rule here. We multiply four by x to the power of three. So the answer is four x to the power of three.

Next we learn the sum rule for differentiation. This rule states that the derivative of a sum of functions is the sum of their derivatives. You differentiate each term separately. For example, the derivative of y plus z is dy/dx plus dz/dx.

Consider the function two x squared plus three x. We use the sum rule here. We differentiate two x squared and then we differentiate three x. The derivative is four x plus three. So the answer is four x plus three.

Finally, we look at the constant multiple rule. This rule says that the derivative of a constant times a function is the constant times the derivative. We keep the constant and differentiate the function part. For example, the derivative of five x squared is five times two x. The answer is ten x squared.

faq.q: What if I have a constant term, like just seven?
faq.a: The derivative of any constant number is always zero. This is because a constant value does not change as x changes. You might also ask what is the derivative of a constant or what is the derivative of a number.
asks: If the function is just a number, what is its derivative?

faq.q: Do I have to use all three rules every time?
faq.a: No, you only use the rules that fit the function you are differentiating. If there are only powers, use the power rule. If there are multiple terms, use the sum rule.
asks: Which rule do I use for x cubed?
Do I need to use all three rules together?

faq.q: Does the constant multiple rule only work for x?
faq.a: No, the constant multiple rule works for any function part. You keep the constant and differentiate the entire function part that follows it. For example, seven times x squared works the same way.
asks: Can I use the constant rule with trig functions?
Does the constant stay outside the derivative?

faq.q: What is the power rule for something like x to the negative two?
faq.a: You apply the power rule exactly the same way. You multiply the power by the term and then subtract one from the original power. So for x to the negative two, you get negative two x to the power of negative three.
asks: How do I differentiate x to the power of negative one?
Can I use the power rule with negative exponents?

faq.q: If I have three parts added together, do I just do it three times?
faq.a: Yes, you use the sum rule repeatedly. You find the derivative of the first part, then add the derivative of the second part, and so on. You differentiate each term independently.
asks: How do I differentiate three terms?
Is it like adding up separate derivatives?

facts: The derivative of x to the power of n is n x to the power of n minus one.
The derivative of a sum of functions is the sum of their individual derivatives.
The derivative of a constant multiplied by a function is the constant times the derivative of the function.
The derivative of x is one.

quiz.say: Find the derivative of x to the power of five.
quiz.why: We use the power rule: five times x to the power of five minus one gives five x to the power of four.

wrong.0: This is the original function, not its derivative.
wrong.1: This incorrectly multiplies the constant by the original term.
wrong.2: This incorrectly reduces the power too much.

quiz.say: Find the derivative of three x cubed plus two x.
quiz.why: We use the sum rule, differentiating three x cubed gives nine x squared, and differentiating two x gives two. Adding them gives nine x squared plus two.

wrong.1: This only differentiates the second term correctly.
wrong.2: This incorrectly applies the power rule to the first term.
wrong.3: This incorrectly leaves the x in the second term.

quiz.say: Find the derivative of seven x squared.
quiz.why: We use the constant multiple rule. We keep the seven and differentiate x squared, which is two x. So we multiply seven by two x to get fourteen x.

wrong.0: This is mathematically correct but less simplified than the expected answer.
wrong.2: This is the original function, ignoring the differentiation.
wrong.3: This incorrectly leaves the power of two on the x.
